intake: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a single exceptionally refined desktop web application screenshot, 16:9 landscape, for Re::Source's first screen. This REPLACES an earlier concept the user rejected as generic AI design. Direction: quiet premium industrial software, the restraint and typographic craft of Apple's professional apps and Linear, understated and confident. This is an actual task-entry screen, not a marketing landing page. Flat almost-black charcoal background #151515, offwhite text, subtle warm-gray secondary text, hairline dividers. No gradients, no glow, no teal, no glass, no large cards, no decorative geometry, no illustrations, NO JET ENGINE, NO PRODUCT RENDER, NO globe, no fake HUD, no slogan, no browser chrome. Highly deliberate spacing and a strong typographic hierarchy. Tiny precise Re::Source wordmark upper left at 56px inset; upper right a quiet 'Help' text link and small circular avatar with A. Thin unobtrusive horizontal hairline below header. Central content column about 540px wide placed slightly left of true centre, around 35% down viewport: small muted breadcrumb 'Workspace / New assembly'; below medium-large editorial sans text 'Start with your design files.' (not gigantic); one restrained sentence 'Add an assembly and its supporting documents.' Below 36px gap, a simple elegant file intake region, no heavy border or chunky box: a fine gray horizontal rule above and below a row with small outline file-plus icon, left text 'Add design package' and smaller 'CAD, parts list and specifications', far right compact offwhite button 'Choose files' with black text, modest 6px radius. Below understated two-line help text 'Drop files here, or choose a folder.' 'Your documents stay together as one assembly.' A small secondary text link below with an arrow: 'Explore a sample assembly →'. Keep the remaining canvas completely quiet and empty. Footer bottom left tiny 'Re::Source' and bottom right small 'Design concept'. Use excellent balanced modern sans-serif typography with natural case and no excessive tracking. All copy sparse, legible, exact. Full page intentionally clean, premium, calm, no AI-generated visual tropes.
style: Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE high-fidelity 16:9 desktop screenshot of Re::Source aerospace sourcing application. Use attached screenshot ONLY as visual-system reference: quiet premium industrial software, flat charcoal #151515, offwhite modern sans-serif typography, warm-gray secondary text, hairline dividers, generous whitespace, refined small neutral buttons, exceptional Apple professional app / Linear restraint. Top-left Re::Source wordmark, top-right Help and small A avatar. No browser chrome, no marketing slogan, no neon, no glow, no glass, no dashboard cards or global tabs, no fake HUD. Later engine renders/map provide functional content, keep typography calm and controls sparse. All data fictional demo fixtures. Bottom-right subtle “Design concept · Demo data”. Render legible exact concise text.

screens.brief: Screen 02 PROCESSING PACKAGE. Keep centre-left editorial heading “Preparing your assembly.” and subtitle “Linking geometry, parts and requirements.” Below slim vertical status list: checked “Assembly identified”, checked “Parts mapped”, active “Linking specifications”, muted “Preparing workspace”. Right two thirds show subtle light-gray technical wireframe of a jet engine on charcoal, just becoming visible as geometry loads, small fine lines, no decorative ornaments. Bottom-left compact filename “engine-assembly.step” with metadata “Design package received”. No arbitrary percentage. Quiet process screen conveying actual work.

Screen 03 EXPLORE ASSEMBLY. Fullscreen engineering canvas with large realistic titanium turbofan jet engine three-quarter side view, visibly exploded into five coherent modules separated modestly along axis. White studio metal highlights, no glow. Small top-left breadcrumb below header “Demo engine / Assembly”. Right slim collapsible parts pane width 280px, neutral dark surface with no heavy border: heading “Components”, three selectable rows “Oil-pump module” selected with subtle pale mint marker, “Fuel-metering unit”, “Starter assembly”. Main oil-pump accessory highlighted subtly and connected with a single thin leader to small label. Bottom-left quiet controls “Rotate   Explode   Reset view”. Large engine fills canvas rather than boxed cards. No additional charts.

Screen 04 SELECT PART AND CONFIRM NEED. Left two-thirds dark engineering canvas with isolated photoreal machined aircraft engine oil-pump module centered large, ghosted engine silhouette behind at very low opacity. Small top-left breadcrumb “Demo engine / Oil-pump module”. Right contextual pane 360px wide, header “Find a replacement”, small line “RS-OP-104 · Rev C”. Form four compact controls: Reason “Faulty component”, Quantity “1”, Required arrival “20 Nov 2026”, Deliver to “Bristol manufacturing site”. Beneath “Exact approved part and revision” with small quiet check. Bottom primary offwhite button “Find suppliers →”. Narrow text “Requirements linked from design package”. Functional precise layout, beautiful unboxed whitespace.

Screen 05 SUPPLIER DISCOVERY. Functional fullscreen dark flat map of Europe and United Kingdom, accurate recognizable coastlines in slightly lighter charcoal, fine subdued borders, sparse city labels. Map takes all canvas below thin header. Top-left under header small unobtrusive selected-part chip with thumbnail of oil-pump module and text “Oil-pump module”, “RS-OP-104 · Rev C”, small expand arrow. Below chip text “Finding supplier sites” and small “Searching part availability and manufacturing capability”. Candidate pins appear around UK, France, Germany, Netherlands and Italy, simple small offwhite dots, a few labelled cities. Bristol delivery destination has distinct small square label “Deliver to Bristol”. At bottom a compact low-height progress strip “Discovering sites” with short source status “Supplier directories · Part catalogues · Site records”. Geography should be calm and expansive; no glowing arcs, no satellite imagery, no heavyweight sidebars yet. Status small line “Demo sourcing scenario”.

Screen 06 AGENTS CHECK CANDIDATES. Same fullscreen dark map of Europe with UK and accurate geographical pins. Top-left persistent small oil-pump thumbnail chip “Oil-pump module”, “RS-OP-104 · Rev C”. A refined floating work panel at centre-right occupies 38% width, matte charcoal slightly lighter than map, subtle border not glass: heading “Checking supplier evidence”. Small summary “12 sites found · 5 excluded · 4 awaiting evidence · 3 eligible”. Below visible task rows: check “Part and revision match”, check “Site qualification”, active “Arrival feasibility”, waiting “Commercial comparison”. Below thin rule a concrete result: “Site excluded”, “Revision B offered; Revision C required”, small evidence link “View source ↗”. Tiny timestamp “Checked just now”. Map outside panel remains visible: excluded pins muted with slash, awaiting pins hollow amber, eligible pins pale mint. Fine short connector highlights one relevant site. Legend bottom-left “Eligible   Awaiting evidence   Excluded” distinguished by symbols as well as subtle colours. No gratuitous graphs or chains of thought. Premium disciplined layout.

Screen 07 SELECT FROM TOP THREE. Fullscreen dark geographic map of UK and western Europe below quiet header. Top-left small persistent component chip thumbnail plus “Oil-pump module / RS-OP-104 · Rev C”. Map left 68% width frames three numbered site pins: 1 Derby UK, 2 Toulouse France, 3 Hamburg Germany. Bristol destination square. Thin subdued routes to destination. Right contextual drawer 32% width full height below header with very deliberate legible hierarchy and fine rules, not cards. Heading “Recommended sites”, three compact rank rows “1  Northline Aero · Derby”, “2  Atelier Turbine · Toulouse”, “3  Hanse Components · Hamburg”; first selected. All supplier names are fictional. Below selected detail heading “Northline Aero”, small “Derby, United Kingdom”. Recommendation block simple type “Recommended for delivery fit” then “Exact revision matched. Shortest estimated route.” concise facts in rows “Part match  RS-OP-104 · Rev C”, “Price estimate  £4,850”, “Estimated arrival  19 Nov”, “Availability  Awaiting supplier confirmation”. Link “Evidence and qualification ↗”. Small “AI recommendation · Based on checked sources”. Fixed bottom button “Select supplier →”. Do not imply estimates are confirmed quotes. Map selected pin remains unobstructed.

Screen 08 DISRUPTION RECHECK. Same fullscreen charcoal map UK and western Europe, tiny selected oil-pump thumbnail top-left with “Oil-pump module / RS-OP-104 · Rev C”. Amber very restrained persistent alert across top below header: small warning icon, “Delivery disruption detected”, second line “Derby dispatch delayed. Arrival now falls after 20 Nov.” small text “Demo event · 10:42”. Affected Derby to Bristol route highlighted amber with a break marker. Other candidate pins stay visible muted. Right contextual 32% pane heading “Rechecking the plan”. Show exact ordered task states: checked “Existing qualifications retained”, active “Check alternate dispatch sites”, waiting “Recalculate arrival dates”, waiting “Update supplier ranking”. Beneath thin rule before-after comparison: “Previous: Derby · 19 Nov” struck subtly then “Updated estimate: 23 Nov · Misses deadline”. Small “Technical requirements unchanged”. Bottom understated action “View previous shortlist”. This shows active rerun rather than resolved result. Precise understated mission control without science fiction graphics. Small footer concept label.

Screen 09 PREPARE FULFILMENT after rerun user selected fictional Atelier Turbine Toulouse. Same quiet premium charcoal style. Top-left small component thumbnail chip “Oil-pump module / RS-OP-104 · Rev C”. Main canvas left column 42% width editorial heading “Prepare the order.” supporting “Atelier Turbine · Toulouse”. Vertical clear workflow with thin linking line: checked “Supplier selected”, active “Review supplier enquiry”, then “Confirm quotation”, “Prepare purchase order”, “Request quality documents”, “Arrange delivery”. Right column 50% width document preview on slightly lighter charcoal (not white paper), heading “Request for quotation” with tiny “DRAFT · DEMO”. Crisp rows “Recipient: Atelier Turbine sales”, “Part: RS-OP-104 · Rev C”, “Quantity: 1”, “Required arrival: 20 Nov 2026”, “Ship to: Bristol manufacturing site”. Attachment lines “Technical requirements.pdf”, “Part applicability.pdf”. Bottom left of document “Prepared for review”, then primary offwhite “Approve simulated send →”. Clear subtle persistent label “Demo mode · No external messages sent”. This is preparation, not confirmed shipment. Generous whitespace, no tiled dashboard or fake chat.

Screen 10 RETURN TO ASSEMBLY. Same restrained premium dark application. Large realistic titanium jet turbofan engine reassembled on left 70% canvas, matching cinematic engineering view with precise metal textures. Oil-pump module subtly selected in pale mint at actual accessory region, single thin leader. Top-left breadcrumb “Demo engine / Recovery preview”. Right narrow 28% pane heading “Replacement matched.” with small “Oil-pump module / RS-OP-104 · Rev C”. Quiet confirmation rows “Part identity matched”, “Evidence linked”, “Delivery plan prepared”. Below thin rule small honest label “Engineering acceptance pending”. Lower primary button “Preview reassembly” and secondary text “View sourcing record ↗”. Under engine bottom left a small status “Restored simulation” with playback icon and subdued note “Visual preview”. No claims actual airworthiness or physical repair. Composition celebrates recovered assembly without confetti, neon or hero slogans. This is conceptual engine simulation after sourcing preparation, not actual shipment.

Screen 08B DISRUPTION RESOLVED AND RERANKED. Same quiet premium Re::Source charcoal desktop app and offwhite typography from reference. Fullscreen map of western Europe left 65%, right supplier comparison drawer 35%. Top-left fixed compact oil-pump thumbnail chip “Oil-pump module”, “RS-OP-104 · Rev C” plus small “Qty 1 · Required 20 Nov · Bristol”. Slim restrained alert under header “Plan updated after Derby dispatch delay”. Map numbered pins now 1 Toulouse, 2 Hamburg, 3 Derby, Bristol destination square. Thin schematic lines from suppliers TOWARD Bristol, selected Toulouse line subtle pale mint. Right drawer heading “Updated recommendation”. Small text “Same requirements. New delivery plan.” Before/after rows separated by rules: “Previously #1: Northline Aero · Derby” followed “Arrival 23 Nov · Misses 20 Nov deadline”, then selected “Now #1: Atelier Turbine · Toulouse”, “Estimated arrival 19 Nov · Within deadline”. Next rows “#2 Hanse Components · Hamburg” and “Derby excluded from on-time shortlist”. Note “Stock and arrival awaiting supplier confirmation”. Small contextual recommendation “Choose Toulouse to preserve the required arrival date.” Primary offwhite button “Review Toulouse supplier →”. All data fictional. Correct route direction toward destination. Calm beautiful typography, no glow no generic dashboard. Small footer “Design concept · Demo data”.
